**Robert Francis Kennedy Jr.** (born January 17, 1954), also known by his initials **RFK Jr.**, is an American politician, [environmental lawyer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_lawyer "Environmental lawyer"), author, [conspiracy theorist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conspiracy_theorist "Conspiracy theorist"), and [anti-vaccine activist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-vaccine_activist "Anti-vaccine activist") serving as the 26th [United States secretary of health and human services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services "United States Secretary of Health and Human Services") since 2025. A member of the prominent [Kennedy family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family "Kennedy family"), he is a son of Senator and US attorney general [Robert F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy "Robert F. Kennedy") and a nephew of US president [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") and US senator [Ted Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy "Ted Kennedy").

Kennedy began his career as an assistant district attorney in [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Manhattan_District_Attorney "Manhattan District Attorney"). In the mid-1980s, he joined two nonprofits focused on [environmental protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_protection "Environmental protection"): [Riverkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverkeeper "Riverkeeper") and the [Natural Resources Defense Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_Resources_Defense_Council "Natural Resources Defense Council") (NRDC). In 1986, he became an adjunct professor of environmental law at [Pace University School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pace_University_School_of_Law "Pace University School of Law"), and in 1987 he founded Pace's Environmental Litigation Clinic. In 1999, Kennedy founded the nonprofit environmental group [Waterkeeper Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterkeeper_Alliance "Waterkeeper Alliance"). He first ran as a member of the [Democratic Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Democratic_Party_(United_States) "Democratic Party (United States)") and later started [an independent campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr._2024_presidential_campaign "Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 2024 presidential campaign") in the [2024 presidential election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"), before withdrawing from the race and endorsing the [Republican Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Republican_Party_(United_States) "Republican Party (United States)")'s nominee, [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump").

Since 2005, Kennedy has promoted [vaccine misinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccine_misinformation "Vaccine misinformation")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFKVaccineMisinformation-1) and public-health conspiracy theories,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFKConspiracySources-2) including the [chemtrail conspiracy theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemtrail_conspiracy_theory "Chemtrail conspiracy theory"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-bbcChemtrails-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chemtrails-cnn-4) [HIV/AIDS denialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS_denialism "HIV/AIDS denialism"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFKAIDS-5) and the scientifically disproved claim of a causal link between [vaccines and autism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccines_and_autism "Vaccines and autism").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-FCRFKAutism-6) He has drawn criticism for fueling [vaccine hesitancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccine_hesitancy "Vaccine hesitancy") amid a social climate that gave rise to the deadly [measles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measles "Measles") outbreaks in [Samoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Samoa_measles_outbreak "2019 Samoa measles outbreak") and [Tonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Tonga_measles_outbreak "2019 Tonga measles outbreak").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-APMeaslesSamoa-7) Kennedy has said that all his children were vaccinated and, during the 2025 measles outbreak, publicly encouraged people to get the measles vaccine.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Kennedy_vaccinated_children-8)[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Kennedy_measles_vaccine-9) Kennedy is the founder and former chairman[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-10) of [Children's Health Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_Health_Defense "Children's Health Defense"), an [anti-vaccine advocacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-vaccine_activism "Anti-vaccine activism") group and proponent of [COVID-19 vaccine misinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_vaccine_misinformation "COVID-19 vaccine misinformation"). He has written books including *[The Riverkeepers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Riverkeepers "The Riverkeepers")* (1997), *[Crimes Against Nature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crimes_Against_Nature_(2004_book) "Crimes Against Nature (2004 book)")* (2004), *[The Real Anthony Fauci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Real_Anthony_Fauci "The Real Anthony Fauci")* (2021), and *[A Letter to Liberals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/A_Letter_to_Liberals "A Letter to Liberals")* (2022).

In November 2024, President-elect Trump nominated Kennedy for secretary of health and human services (HHS). In February 2025, the Senate confirmed Kennedy by a vote of 52 to 48, and he was sworn in shortly thereafter amid strong opposition from scientists and medical groups. His tenure has been marked by controversial actions on vaccines, public [health policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_policy "Health policy"), and agency leadership that have drawn significant legal, scientific, and political criticism.

## Early life and education

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/President_John_F._Kennedy_with_Robert_F._Kennedy%2C_Jr._%2802%29.jpg/250px-President_John_F._Kennedy_with_Robert_F._Kennedy%2C_Jr._%2802%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:President_John_F._Kennedy_with_Robert_F._Kennedy,_Jr._(02).jpg)Seven-year old Kennedy with his uncle, President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy"), in the [Oval Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office") in 1961

Robert Francis Kennedy Jr. was born at Georgetown University Hospital in Washington, D.C., on January 17, 1954. He is the third of eleven children of senator and US attorney general [Robert F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy "Robert F. Kennedy") and [Ethel Skakel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethel_Skakel "Ethel Skakel"). He is a nephew of President [John F. Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy "John F. Kennedy") and Senator [Ted Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy "Ted Kennedy").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOppenheimer20155–6-11)

Kennedy was raised at the [Kennedy Compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Compound "Kennedy Compound") in [Hyannis Port, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyannis_Port,_Massachusetts "Hyannis Port, Massachusetts"), and at [Hickory Hill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hickory_Hill_(McLean,_Virginia) "Hickory Hill (McLean, Virginia)"), the family estate in [McLean, Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/McLean,_Virginia "McLean, Virginia").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-12)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-14) In June 1972, he graduated from the Palfrey Street School, a day school in [Watertown, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watertown,_Massachusetts "Watertown, Massachusetts"). While attending Palfrey, he lived with a surrogate family at a farmhouse in [Cambridge, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambridge,_Massachusetts "Cambridge, Massachusetts").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-15) Kennedy continued his education at [Harvard University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_University "Harvard University"), graduating in 1976 with a Bachelor of Arts in American history and literature. With his former roommate [Peter W. Kaplan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_W._Kaplan "Peter W. Kaplan"), he did thesis research in Alabama.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-16) He earned a [Juris Doctor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juris_Doctor "Juris Doctor") degree from the [University of Virginia School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Virginia_School_of_Law "University of Virginia School of Law") in 1982[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Moore_3/26/2025-18) and a [Master of Laws](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Master_of_Laws "Master of Laws") from [Pace University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pace_University "Pace University") in 1987.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-19)

He was nine years old when John F. Kennedy [was assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_John_F._Kennedy "Assassination of John F. Kennedy") in 1963, and 14 when his father [was assassinated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assassination_of_Robert_F._Kennedy "Assassination of Robert F. Kennedy") while running for president in 1968.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOppenheimer201527-20) Kennedy learned of his father's shooting while at [Georgetown Preparatory School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Georgetown_Preparatory_School "Georgetown Preparatory School").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-21) A few hours later, he flew to Los Angeles on Vice President [Hubert Humphrey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_Humphrey "Hubert Humphrey")'s plane, along with his older siblings, [Kathleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kathleen_Kennedy_Townsend "Kathleen Kennedy Townsend") and [Joseph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joseph_P._Kennedy_II "Joseph P. Kennedy II"). He was with his father when he died. Kennedy was a pallbearer at his father's funeral, where he spoke and read excerpts from his father's speeches at the mass commemorating his death at [Arlington National Cemetery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arlington_National_Cemetery "Arlington National Cemetery").[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-22)[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-23)

After his father's death, Kennedy struggled with drug abuse, which led to his arrest in [Barnstable, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barnstable,_Massachusetts "Barnstable, Massachusetts"), for [cannabis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cannabis_(drug) "Cannabis (drug)") possession at age 16,[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-24)[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-25) and his expulsion from two boarding schools: [Millbrook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millbrook_School "Millbrook School") and [Pomfret](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pomfret_School "Pomfret School").[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-27) During this time, some in the Kennedy family regarded him as the "ringleader" of a pack of spoiled, rich kids who called themselves the "Hyannis Port Terrors", engaging in vandalism, theft, and drug use.[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-FOOTNOTEOppenheimer201566-29) His first cousin [Caroline Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroline_Kennedy "Caroline Kennedy") later blamed Kennedy for leading other members of their family "down the path of drug addiction", calling him a "predator".[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-30) At Harvard, Kennedy continued to use [heroin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroin "Heroin") and [cocaine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cocaine "Cocaine"), often with his brother David, earning a reputation that has been described as a "pied piper" and "drug dealer".[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hagan_20240702-32)

In 1972, Kennedy and [Roger Ailes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roger_Ailes "Roger Ailes") made a film about wildlife and conservation in Kenya.[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-33)[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-34)[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-35) Kennedy's book on [Frank Minis Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frank_Minis_Johnson "Frank Minis Johnson"), a federal judge who led [racial desegregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desegregation_in_the_United_States "Desegregation in the United States") in Alabama, was published in 1978.[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-36)[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-37)[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-39)

## Career

### Manhattan DA's office

In 1982, Kennedy was sworn in as an [assistant district attorney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Assistant_district_attorney "Assistant district attorney") for [Manhattan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_County_District_Attorney "New York County District Attorney").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-KW-40) After failing the New York [bar exam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bar_examination_in_the_United_States "Bar examination in the United States"), he resigned in July 1983.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-UPI1989-41)

### Conviction for heroin possession

On September 16, 1983, Kennedy was arrested and charged with [heroin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heroin "Heroin") possession in [Rapid City, South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rapid_City,_South_Dakota "Rapid City, South Dakota"), after he fell ill in an airplane bathroom.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-UPI1989-41) In February 1984, he pleaded guilty to a single [felony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felony "Felony") charge of possession of heroin, and was sentenced to two years of [probation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probation "Probation") and community service.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-heroin-42)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-living-dangerously-43) After his arrest, he entered a drug treatment center.[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-UPI1989-41) To satisfy conditions of his probation, Kennedy worked as a volunteer for the [Natural Resources Defense Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_Resources_Defense_Council "Natural Resources Defense Council") (NRDC) and was required to attend regular drug rehabilitation sessions.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-QuietVictory-44) Kennedy asserted that this ended his 14 years of heroin use, which he said had begun when he was 15.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hagan_20240702-32) His probation ended a year early.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-QuietVictory-44)

### Riverkeeper

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3d/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr._flying_a_Harris_Hawk_with_his_daughter%2C_Kick_Kennedy_%281989%29.jpg/250px-Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr._flying_a_Harris_Hawk_with_his_daughter%2C_Kick_Kennedy_%281989%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr._flying_a_Harris_Hawk_with_his_daughter,_Kick_Kennedy_(1989).jpg)Kennedy with his daughter, Kick, holding a [Harris's hawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harris's_hawk "Harris's hawk") in 1989

In 1984, Kennedy began volunteering at the Hudson River Fisherman's Association, renamed [Riverkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Riverkeeper "Riverkeeper") in 1986 after a patrol boat it had built with settlement money from legal victories preceding Kennedy's arrival.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-46) After he was admitted to the New York bar in 1985, Riverkeeper hired him as senior attorney.[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-QuietVictory-44)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto4-47) Kennedy litigated and supervised [environmental enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_law "Environmental law") lawsuits on the east coast estuaries on behalf of Hudson Riverkeeper and the [Long Island Soundkeeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soundkeeper "Soundkeeper"),[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-48) where he was also a board member. Long Island Soundkeeper sued several municipalities and cities along the Connecticut and New York coastlines.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-49) On the Hudson, Kennedy sued municipalities and industries, including [General Electric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/General_Electric "General Electric"), to stop discharging pollution and clean up legacy contamination.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:2-50) His work at Riverkeeper set long-term environmental legal standards.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:2-50)

In 1995, Kennedy advocated for repeal of legislation that he considered unfriendly to the environment.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto-51) In 1997, he worked with John Cronin to write *The Riverkeepers*, a history of the early Riverkeepers and a primer for the Waterkeeper movement.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto4-47)

In 2000, a majority of Riverkeeper's board sided with Kennedy when he insisted on rehiring William Wegner, a wildlife lecturer and falcon trainer[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-smuggler-52)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45) whom the organization's founder and president, [Robert H. Boyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_H._Boyle "Robert H. Boyle"), had fired six months earlier after learning that Wegner had been convicted in 1995 for tax fraud, perjury, and conspiracy to violate wildlife protection laws.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-rare_egg-53) Wegner had recruited and led a team of at least 10 who smuggled [cockatoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cockatoo "Cockatoo") eggs, including species considered endangered by Australia, from Australia to the US over a period of eight years.[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-smuggler-52)[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45) He served 3.5 years of a five-year sentence and was hired by Kennedy a few months after his release.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45) After the board's decision, Boyle, eight of the 22 members of the board, and Riverkeeper's treasurer resigned, saying it was not right for an environmental organization to hire someone convicted of environmental crimes and that it would hurt the organization's fundraising.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-rare_egg-53)

While working with Riverkeeper, Kennedy spearheaded a 34-year battle to close the [Indian Point](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Point_Energy_Center "Indian Point Energy Center") nuclear-power plant.[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:7-54) Kennedy was featured in a 2004 documentary about the plant, *Indian Point: Imagining the Unimaginable*, directed by his sister, the documentary filmmaker [Rory Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rory_Kennedy "Rory Kennedy").[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-55) In 2017, Kennedy argued that the electricity Indian Point provided could be fully replaced by [renewable energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renewable_energy "Renewable energy").[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:7-54) In 2022, after the plant's closure, carbon emissions from electricity generation in New York state increased by 37%, compared to 2019, before the start of the closure.[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-56)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-57)

Kennedy resigned from Riverkeeper in 2017.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-cockatoo-45)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-58)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-59)

### Pace Environmental Litigation Clinic

In 1987, Kennedy founded the Environmental Litigation Clinic at Pace University School of Law,[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-60) where for three decades he was the clinic's supervising attorney and co-director and Clinical Professor of Law.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-61)[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-62) Kennedy obtained a special order from the New York State Court of Appeals that permitted his 10 clinic students to practice law and try cases against Hudson River polluters in state and federal court, under the supervision of Kennedy and his co-director, Professor Karl Coplan. The clinic's full-time clients are Riverkeeper and Long Island Soundkeeper.[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-oregon-63)

The clinic has sued governments and companies for polluting Long Island Sound and the [Hudson River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River") and its tributaries.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-64) It argued cases to expand citizen access to the shoreline and won hundreds of settlements for the Hudson Riverkeeper.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-65) Kennedy and his students also sued dozens of municipal wastewater treatment plants to force compliance with the [Clean Water Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Water_Act "Clean Water Act").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-oregon-63) In 2010, a Pace lawsuit forced [ExxonMobil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ExxonMobil "ExxonMobil") to clean up tens of millions of gallons of oil from legacy refinery spills in [Newtown Creek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Newtown_Creek "Newtown Creek") in Brooklyn.[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-66)

On April 11, 2001, *[Men's Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Men's_Journal "Men's Journal")* gave Kennedy its "Heroes" Award for creating the Pace Environmental Litigation Clinic.[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-67) Kennedy and the clinic received other awards for successful legal work cleaning up the environment.[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-68) The Pace Clinic became a model for similar environmental law clinics throughout the country.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-69)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-70)[[71]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-71)[[72]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-72)

### Waterkeeper Alliance

In June 1999, as Riverkeeper's success on the Hudson began inspiring the creation of Waterkeepers across North America, Kennedy and a few dozen Riverkeepers gathered in Southampton, Long Island, to found the [Waterkeeper Alliance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Waterkeeper_Alliance "Waterkeeper Alliance"), which is now the umbrella group for the 344 licensed Waterkeeper programs[[73]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-73) in 44 countries.[[74]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-74) As president, Kennedy oversaw its legal, membership, policy and fundraising programs. The Alliance is dedicated to promoting "swimmable, fishable, drinkable waterways, worldwide".[[75]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-75)

Under Kennedy's leadership, Waterkeeper launched its "[Clean Coal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_Coal "Clean Coal") is a Deadly Lie"[[76]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-76) campaign in 2001, bringing dozens of lawsuits targeting mining practices, including [mountaintop removal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mountaintop_removal "Mountaintop removal")[[77]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-77) and [slurry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slurry "Slurry") pond construction, as well as coal-burning utilities' mercury emissions and [coal ash](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coal_ash "Coal ash") piles.[[78]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-78) Kennedy's Waterkeeper alliance has also been fighting coal export, including from terminals in the [Pacific Northwest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Northwest "Pacific Northwest").[[79]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-79)

Waterkeeper waged a legal and public relations battle against pollution from [factory farms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Factory_farm "Factory farm"). In the 1990s, Kennedy rallied opposition to factory farms among small independent farmers, convened a series of "National Summits" on factory meat products, and conducted press conference whistle-stop tours across North Carolina, Iowa, Kansas, Missouri, Illinois, Ohio, and in Washington, D.C. Beginning in 2000, Kennedy sued factory farms in North Carolina, Oklahoma, Maryland, and Iowa.[[80]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-porkchop-80) In a 2003 article, he argued factory farms produce lower-quality, less healthy food, and harm independent family farmers by poisoning their air and water, reducing their property values, and using extensive state and federal subsidies to impose unfair competition against them.[[81]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-81)

Kennedy and his environmental work have been the focus of several films, including *The Waterkeepers* (2000),[[82]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-82) directed by [Les Guthman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Les_Guthman "Les Guthman"). In 2008, he appeared in the [IMAX](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IMAX "IMAX") documentary film *[Grand Canyon Adventure: River at Risk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grand_Canyon_Adventure:_River_at_Risk "Grand Canyon Adventure: River at Risk")*, riding the Grand Canyon in a wooden dory with his daughter Kick and anthropologist [Wade Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wade_Davis_(anthropologist) "Wade Davis (anthropologist)").[[83]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-83)

Kennedy resigned the Waterkeeper Alliance presidency in November 2020.[[84]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-84)

### New York City Watershed Agreement

Beginning in 1991, Kennedy represented environmentalists and New York City watershed consumers in a series of lawsuits against New York City and upstate watershed polluters. Kennedy authored a series of articles and reports[[85]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-watershed-85)[[86]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-86)[[87]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-87)[[88]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-88) alleging that New York State was abdicating its responsibility to protect the water repository and supply. In 1996, he helped orchestrate the $1.2 billion New York City Watershed Agreement, which *[New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(magazine) "New York (magazine)")* magazine recognized in its cover story, "The Kennedy Who Matters".[[89]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-89) This agreement, which Kennedy negotiated on behalf of environmentalists and New York City watershed consumers, is regarded as an international model in stakeholder consensus negotiations and sustainable development.[[90]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-90)

### Kennedy & Madonna LLP

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/R.F.K._jr_2000.jpg/250px-R.F.K._jr_2000.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:R.F.K._jr_2000.jpg)Kennedy in 2000

In 2000, Kennedy and the environmental lawyer Kevin Madonna founded the [environmental law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmental_law "Environmental law") firm Kennedy & Madonna, LLP, to represent private plaintiffs against polluters.[[91]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-KandMTeam-91) The firm litigates environmental contamination cases on behalf of individuals, non-profit organizations, school districts, public water suppliers, Indian tribes, municipalities and states. In 2001, Kennedy & Madonna organized a team of prestigious plaintiff law firms to challenge pollution from industrial pork and poultry production.[[92]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-92) In 2004, the firm was part of a legal team that secured a $70 million settlement for property owners in Pensacola, Florida whose properties were contaminated by chemicals from an adjacent [Superfund](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superfund "Superfund") site.[[93]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-93)

Kennedy & Madonna was profiled in the 2010 HBO documentary *Mann v. Ford*,[[94]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-94) which chronicles four years of litigation by the firm on behalf of the [Ramapough Mountain Indians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ramapough_Mountain_Indians "Ramapough Mountain Indians") against the [Ford Motor Company](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ford_Motor_Company "Ford Motor Company") for dumping toxic waste on tribal lands in northern New Jersey.[[95]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-95) In addition to a monetary settlement for the tribe, the lawsuit contributed to the community's land being relisted on the federal Superfund list, the first time that a delisted site was relisted.[[96]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-96)

In 2007, Kennedy was one of three finalists nominated by Public Justice as "Trial Lawyer of the Year" for his role in the $396 million jury verdict against [DuPont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DuPont "DuPont") for contamination from its zinc plant in [Spelter, West Virginia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spelter,_West_Virginia "Spelter, West Virginia").[[97]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-97) In 2017, the firm was part of the trial team that secured a $670 million settlement on behalf of over 3,000 residents from Ohio and West Virginia whose drinking water was contaminated by the toxic chemical [perfluorooctanoic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perfluorooctanoic_acid "Perfluorooctanoic acid"), which DuPont released into the environment in [Parkersburg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parkersburg "Parkersburg"), West Virginia.[[98]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-98)

### Morgan & Morgan

In 2016, Kennedy became counsel to the [Morgan & Morgan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morgan_&_Morgan "Morgan & Morgan") law firm.[[99]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-99) The partnership arose from the two firms' successful collaboration on the case against SoCalGas Company following the [Aliso Canyon gas leak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aliso_Canyon_gas_leak "Aliso Canyon gas leak") in California.[[100]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-100) In 2017, Kennedy and his partners sued [Monsanto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monsanto "Monsanto") in federal court in San Francisco, on behalf of plaintiffs seeking to recover damages for [non-Hodgkin's lymphoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Hodgkin's_lymphoma "Non-Hodgkin's lymphoma") cases that, the plaintiffs allege, were a result of exposure to Monsanto's [glyphosate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glyphosate "Glyphosate")-based herbicide, [Roundup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roundup_(herbicide) "Roundup (herbicide)"). Kennedy and his team also filed a class action lawsuit against Monsanto for failing to warn consumers about the dangers allegedly posed by exposure to Roundup.[[101]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-101)

In September 2018, Kennedy and his partners filed a class-action lawsuit against [Columbia Gas of Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Gas_of_Massachusetts "Columbia Gas of Massachusetts") alleging negligence following [gas explosions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merrimack_Valley_gas_explosions "Merrimack Valley gas explosions") in three towns north of Boston. Of Columbia Gas, Kennedy said, "as they build new miles of pipe, the same company is ignoring its existing infrastructure, which we now know is eroding and is dilapidated".[[102]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-102)

### Cape Wind

Main article: [Cape Wind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Wind "Cape Wind")

In 2005, Kennedy clashed with national environmental groups over his opposition to the Cape Wind Project, a proposed [offshore wind farm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offshore_wind_farm "Offshore wind farm") in [Cape Cod, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod,_Massachusetts "Cape Cod, Massachusetts") (in [Nantucket Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nantucket_Sound "Nantucket Sound")). Taking the side of Cape Cod's commercial [fishing industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishing_industry "Fishing industry"), Kennedy argued that the project was a costly boondoggle. This position angered some environmentalists, and Kennedy was criticized by [Rush Limbaugh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rush_Limbaugh "Rush Limbaugh") and [John Stossel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Stossel "John Stossel").[*[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")*] In *[The Wall Street Journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wall_Street_Journal "The Wall Street Journal")*, Kennedy wrote, "Vermont wants to take its nuclear plant off line and replace it with clean, green power from Hydro-Québec—power available to Massachusetts utilities—at a cost of six cents per kilowatt hour (kwh). Cape Wind electricity, by a conservative estimate and based on figures they filed with the state, comes in at 25 cents per kwh."[[103]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-103)

### Other ventures

In 1999, Kennedy, Chris Bartle and John Hoving created a bottled water company, Keeper Springs, which donated all of its profits to Waterkeeper Alliance.[[104]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-104)

Kennedy was a venture partner and senior advisor at VantagePoint Capital Partners, one of the world's largest [cleantech](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clean_technology "Clean technology") [venture capital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venture_capital "Venture capital") firms. Among other activities, VantagePoint was the original and largest pre-[IPO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/IPO "IPO") institutional investor in [Tesla, Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tesla,_Inc. "Tesla, Inc.")[[105]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-105) VantagePoint also backed BrightSource Energy and Solazyme, amongst others. Kennedy is a board member and counselor to several of Vantage Point's portfolio companies in the water and energy space, including Ostara, a Vancouver-based company that markets the technology to remove [phosphorus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphorus "Phosphorus") and other excessive nutrients from [wastewater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wastewater "Wastewater"), transforming otherwise pollution directly into high-grade fertilizer.[[106]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-106) He is also a senior advisor to Starwood Energy Group and has played a key role in a number of the firm's investments.[[107]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-107)

He is on the board of Vionx, a Massachusetts-based utility-scale [vanadium flow battery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanadium_flow_battery "Vanadium flow battery") systems manufacturer. On October 5, 2017, Vionx, [National Grid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Grid_plc "National Grid plc") and the [US Department of Energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Energy "United States Department of Energy") completed the installation of advanced flow batteries at [Holy Name High School](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holy_Name_Central_Catholic_High_School "Holy Name Central Catholic High School") in the city of [Worcester, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Worcester,_Massachusetts "Worcester, Massachusetts"). The collaboration also includes [Siemens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siemens "Siemens") and the [United Technologies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Technologies "United Technologies") Research Center and constitutes one of the largest energy storage facilities in Massachusetts.[[108]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-108)

Kennedy served on the board of the New York [League of Conservation Voters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/League_of_Conservation_Voters "League of Conservation Voters").[[109]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-109)

Kennedy is a partner in ColorZen, which offers a turnkey-cotton-fiber pre-treatment solution that reduces water usage and toxic discharges in the [cotton-dyeing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dyeing "Dyeing") process.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hilburn-3_Jun_2016-110)[[111]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-111)[[112]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-112)

Kennedy was a co-owner and director of the [smart-grid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smart_grid "Smart grid") company Utility Integration Solutions (UISol),[[113]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-113) which was acquired by [Alstom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alstom "Alstom"). He is presently a co-owner and director of GridBright, the market-leading grid management specialist.[[114]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-114)

In October 2011, Kennedy co-founded *EcoWatch*, an environmental news site.[[115]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-115) He resigned from its board of directors in 2018.[[116]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-116)

### Minority and poor communities

In his first case as an environmental attorney, Kennedy represented the [NAACP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NAACP "NAACP") in a lawsuit against a proposal to build a garbage transfer station in a minority neighborhood in [Ossining, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ossining,_New_York_(village) "Ossining, New York (village)").[[117]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-117) In 1987, he successfully sued [Westchester County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Westchester_County "Westchester County") to reopen the [Croton Point Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Croton_Point_Park "Croton Point Park"), which was primarily used by poor and minority communities from [the Bronx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bronx "The Bronx").[[118]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-118) He then forced the reopening of the [Pelham Bay Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelham_Bay_Park "Pelham Bay Park"), which New York City had closed to the public and converted to a police firing range.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto4-47)

### International and indigenous rights

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/2d/UFW%27s_ARturo_Rodriguez_%26_Robert_Kennedy_Jr._%2832424580442%29.jpg/250px-UFW%27s_ARturo_Rodriguez_%26_Robert_Kennedy_Jr._%2832424580442%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:UFW's_ARturo_Rodriguez_&_Robert_Kennedy_Jr._(32424580442).jpg)Kennedy at a [United Farm Workers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_Farm_Workers "United Farm Workers") rally in 2017

Starting in 1985, Kennedy helped develop the international program for environmental, energy, and human rights of the [Natural Resources Defense Council](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Natural_Resources_Defense_Council "Natural Resources Defense Council") (NRDC), traveling to Canada and Latin America to assist indigenous tribes in protecting their homelands and opposing large-scale energy and extractive projects in remote wilderness areas.[[119]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-119)

In 1990, Kennedy assisted indigenous [Pehuenches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pehuenche "Pehuenche") in Chile in a partially successful campaign to stop the construction of a series of dams on Chile's iconic [Biobío River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biobío_River "Biobío River"). That campaign derailed all but one of the proposed dams.[[120]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-120) Beginning in 1992, he assisted the [Cree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cree "Cree") Indians of northern Quebec in their campaign against Hydro-Québec to halt construction of some 600 proposed dams on eleven rivers in [James Bay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_Bay "James Bay").[[121]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-121)

In 1993, Kennedy and NRDC, working with the indigenous rights organization [Cultural Survival](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_Survival "Cultural Survival"), clashed with other American environmental groups in a dispute about the rights of Indians to govern their own lands in the [Oriente](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oriente_(Ecuador) "Oriente (Ecuador)") region of Ecuador.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto6-122) Kennedy represented the [CONFENIAE](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONFENIAE "CONFENIAE"), a confederation of indigenous peoples, in negotiation with the American oil company [Conoco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conoco "Conoco") to limit oil development in Ecuadorian Amazon and, at the same time, obtain benefits from resource extraction for Amazonian tribes.[[122]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto6-122) Kennedy was a vocal critic of [Texaco](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texaco "Texaco") for its previous record of polluting the [Ecuadoran Amazon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecuadorian_Amazon "Ecuadorian Amazon").[[123]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-123)

From 1993 to 1999, Kennedy worked with five [Vancouver Island](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vancouver_Island "Vancouver Island") First Nations in their campaign to end industrial logging by [MacMillan Bloedel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MacMillan_Bloedel "MacMillan Bloedel") in [Clayoquot Sound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clayoquot_Sound "Clayoquot Sound"), British Columbia.[[124]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-124) In 1996, he met with Cuban president [Fidel Castro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fidel_Castro "Fidel Castro") to persuade him to halt his plans to construct a nuclear power plant at [Juraguá](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juraguá "Juraguá").[[125]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-125) During the meeting, Castro reminisced about Kennedy's father and uncle, speculating that US relations with Cuba would have been far better had President Kennedy not been assassinated.[[126]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-126)

Between 1996 and 2000, Kennedy and the NRDC helped Mexican commercial fishermen halt [Mitsubishi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitsubishi "Mitsubishi")'s proposal to build a salt facility in the [Laguna San Ignacio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laguna_San_Ignacio "Laguna San Ignacio"), an area in Baja where [gray whales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray_whale "Gray whale") breed and nurse their calves.[[127]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-127) Kennedy wrote in opposition to the project, and took the campaign to Japan, meeting with [Japanese Prime Minister](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Japan "Prime Minister of Japan") [Keizo Obuchi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keizo_Obuchi "Keizo Obuchi").[[128]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-128) In 2000, he assisted local environmental activists to stop Chaffin Light, a real estate developer, and US engineering giant [Bechtel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bechtel "Bechtel") from building a large hotel and resort development that, Kennedy argued, threatened [coral reefs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral_reef "Coral reef") and public beaches used by local Bahamians, at Clifton Bay, [New Providence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Providence "New Providence") Island.[[129]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-129)

Kennedy was one of the early editors of *[Indian Country Today](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Country_Today "Indian Country Today")*, North America's largest [Native American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indigenous_peoples_of_the_Americas "Indigenous peoples of the Americas") newspaper.[[130]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-130) He helped lead the opposition to the damming of the [Futaleufú River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Futaleufú_River "Futaleufú River") in the [Southern Zone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zona_Sur "Zona Sur") of Chile.[[131]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-131) In 2016, due to the pressure precipitated by the Futaleufú Riverkeepers campaign against the dams, the Spanish power company [Endesa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endesa "Endesa"), which owned the right to dam the river, reversed its decision and relinquished all claims to the Futaleufú.[[132]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-132)

### Military and Vieques

Kennedy has been a critic of environmental damage by the US military.[[133]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-133)[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFK_Jr.-16_May_2003-134)

In a 2001 article, Kennedy described how he sued the [US Navy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Navy "US Navy") on behalf of fishermen and residents of [Vieques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vieques "Vieques"), an island of [Puerto Rico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puerto_Rico "Puerto Rico"), to stop weapons testing, bombing, and other military exercises. Kennedy argued that the activities were unnecessary, and that the Navy had illegally destroyed several endangered species, polluted the island's waters, harmed the residents' health, and damaged its economy.[[135]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-vieques-135) He was arrested for trespassing at [Camp Garcia Vieques](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camp_Garcia_Vieques "Camp Garcia Vieques"), the US Navy training facility, where he and others were protesting the use of a section of the island for training. Kennedy served 30 days in a maximum security prison in Puerto Rico.[[136]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-136)

The trespassing incident forced the suspension of [live-fire exercises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live-fire_exercise "Live-fire exercise") for almost three hours.[[137]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-137) The lawsuits and protests by Kennedy, and hundreds of Puerto Ricans who were also imprisoned, eventually forced the termination of naval bombing in Vieques by [the Bush administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Presidency_of_George_W._Bush "Presidency of George W. Bush").[[138]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-138)

In a 2003 article for the *[Chicago Tribune](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chicago_Tribune "Chicago Tribune")*, Kennedy called the US federal government "America's biggest polluter" and the [US Department of Defense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Defense "United States Department of Defense") the worst offender. Citing the [Environmental Protection Agency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Environmental_Protection_Agency "United States Environmental Protection Agency") (EPA), he wrote, "unexploded ordnance waste can be found on 16,000 military ranges ... and more than half may contain biological or chemical weapons."[[134]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFK_Jr.-16_May_2003-134)

## Political aspirations

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/73/Nick_DNC_etown.jpg/250px-Nick_DNC_etown.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nick_DNC_etown.jpg)Kennedy at a taping of [eTown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ETown "ETown") during the [2008 Democratic National Convention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Democratic_National_Convention "2008 Democratic National Convention")

### Candidacy aspirations

Kennedy considered running for political office [in 2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_Senate_election_in_New_York "2000 United States Senate election in New York") when [Daniel Patrick Moynihan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Patrick_Moynihan "Daniel Patrick Moynihan"), a [US senator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") from New York, did not seek reelection to the [seat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_United_States_senators_from_New_York "List of United States senators from New York") formerly held by Kennedy's father.[[139]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-139)

In 2005, Kennedy considered running for New York attorney general in the [2006 election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_New_York_Attorney_General_election "2006 New York Attorney General election"), which would have put him up against his then-brother-in-law [Andrew Cuomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Cuomo "Andrew Cuomo"), but he ultimately chose not to, despite being considered the front-runner.[[140]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-140)

On December 2, 2008, Kennedy said he did not want New York governor [David Paterson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/David_Paterson "David Paterson") to nominate him to the US Senate seat to be vacated by [Hillary Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hillary_Clinton "Hillary Clinton"), Obama's nominee for [Secretary of State](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_State "United States Secretary of State"). Some outlets indicated that Kennedy was a possible candidate for the position. He said that Senate service would leave him too little time with his family.[[141]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-141)

### 2000s consideration for top environmental jobs

As a "well-respected climate lawyer" in the 2000s,[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:4-142) Kennedy was "often linked to top environmental jobs in Democratic administrations", including in the [2000](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2000_United_States_presidential_election "2000 United States presidential election"), [2004](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2004_United_States_presidential_election "2004 United States presidential election"), and [2008 presidential elections](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_United_States_presidential_election "2008 United States presidential election").[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:5-143) He was considered as a potential chair of the [White House Council on Environmental Quality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_Council_on_Environmental_Quality "White House Council on Environmental Quality") for [Al Gore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al_Gore "Al Gore") in 2000 and considered for the role of [EPA administrator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Administrator_of_the_Environmental_Protection_Agency "Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency") under [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry") in 2004 and [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") in 2008.[[143]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:5-143)

According to *[Politico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Politico "Politico")*, the Obama transition team decided not to nominate Kennedy due to his past heroin conviction and opposition from Senate Republicans. Then [United States Chamber of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Chamber_of_Commerce "United States Chamber of Commerce") lobbyist [William Kovacs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Kovacic "William Kovacic") said that Kennedy's nomination "would speak volumes as to where Obama is going with his appointments ... A Kennedy appointment is as liberal as you can possibly get ... There is no one [candidate] based firmer in extremes."[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:4-142) Republican Senator [Jim Inhofe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jim_Inhofe "Jim Inhofe") of Oklahoma also criticized the proposal, saying Kennedy was too radical and would further a left-wing agenda if appointed.[[142]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:4-142)

### 2024 presidential campaign

Main article: [Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 2024 presidential campaign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr._2024_presidential_campaign "Robert F. Kennedy Jr. 2024 presidential campaign")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b8/Robert_F._Kennedy%2C_Jr._with_supporter_%2853514292813%29.jpg/250px-Robert_F._Kennedy%2C_Jr._with_supporter_%2853514292813%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Robert_F._Kennedy,_Jr._with_supporter_(53514292813).jpg)Kennedy with a supporter during his 2024 campaign

In a speech in New Hampshire on March 3, 2023, Kennedy said he was considering a [run for president in 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_United_States_presidential_election "2024 United States presidential election"): "I am thinking about it. I've passed the biggest hurdle, which is that my wife has greenlighted it."[[144]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-foxmarch3-144)

Kennedy filed his candidacy for the [Democratic presidential nomination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_Democratic_Party_presidential_primaries "2024 Democratic Party presidential primaries") on April 5, 2023.[[145]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-145) He formally declared his candidacy at a campaign launch event at the [Park Plaza Hotel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston_Park_Plaza "Boston Park Plaza") in [Boston](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston "Boston") on April 19.[[146]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-146) On October 9, he became an [independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_politician "Independent politician") candidate [in the election](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third-party_and_independent_candidates_for_the_2024_United_States_presidential_election "Third-party and independent candidates for the 2024 United States presidential election").[[147]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-147) He is the fifth member of his family to seek the presidency.[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-kennedy_family-151)

Listing many false conspiracy theories that Kennedy used during campaign appearances, [PolitiFact](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PolitiFact "PolitiFact") named his presidential campaign its 2023 "lie of the year".[[151]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-PolitiFactLOTY2023-152)

In May 2024, Kennedy was considered for the [Libertarian Party's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_(United_States) "Libertarian Party (United States)") nomination for president, but lost to [Chase Oliver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chase_Oliver "Chase Oliver").[[152]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-153) In Colorado, the state [Libertarian Party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Libertarian_Party_of_Colorado "Libertarian Party of Colorado") selected Kennedy, but Oliver appeared on the ballot as the Libertarian nominee.[[153]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-154)[[154]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-155)

Kennedy's campaign was noted for receiving significant support from Republican donors and Trump allies who believed he would serve as a "[spoiler](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spoiler_effect "Spoiler effect")", taking the votes of those who would have otherwise voted for the Democratic nominee.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-NYTApril10-156) In August 2023, it was revealed that [Timothy Mellon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothy_Mellon "Timothy Mellon"), who gave $15 million to [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump")'s [super PAC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Super_PAC "Super PAC") [MAGA Inc.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_America_Great_Again_Inc. "Make America Great Again Inc."), also donated $5 million to Kennedy's super PAC, making him Kennedy's largest single donor.[[155]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-NYTApril10-156)[[156]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-157) Mellon donated another $5 million to Kennedy's super PAC in April and another $50 million to MAGA Inc. in May.[[157]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-158)[[158]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-donor-159) In July 2024, Forbes reported that Mellon had donated $25 million to Kennedy and Kennedy-affiliated groups.[[159]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-160)

In August, facing declining poll numbers, limited campaign funds, and increasing challenges to ballot access, the Kennedy campaign began appealing to the Harris and Trump campaigns, seeking a cabinet post in exchange for an endorsement. Harris reportedly rebuffed Kennedy,[[160]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-161) but Trump said he "probably would [consider the offer], if something like that would happen".[[161]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-162) On August 22, the Kennedy campaign filed to be removed from the Arizona ballot amid reports he would drop out to endorse Trump.[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-163)

On August 23, Kennedy dropped out and endorsed Trump, saying he intended to maintain ballot placement in certain non-[swing states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swing_state "Swing state").[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-NBCEndorsed-164)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-AP2024-08-23-165)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-166) This was a reversal for Kennedy, who had previously said he would "under no circumstances" join Trump on a presidential ticket, that his and Trump's positions "could not be further apart", and that Trump was a "terrible human being", a "discredit to democracy", and "probably a sociopath".[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-167)[[167]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-kennedytrump-168)[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-AP2024-08-23-165) In his speech endorsing Trump, Kennedy described speaking with Trump and his advisers and said he discovered that he and Trump were "aligned on many key issues".[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-NBCEndorsed-164)

In December, Kennedy was featured in the documentary film *[Inactive, Americaʼs Silent Killer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inactive,_Americaʼs_Silent_Killer "Inactive, Americaʼs Silent Killer")*, about the growing global epidemic of physical inactivity and its impact on health, particularly in North America.[[168]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RadioCanada-169)

## Secretary of Health and Human Services (2025–present)

### Nomination and confirmation

hearings.[[173]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-174)[[174]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-175)[[175]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-176) Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Health,_Education,_Labor_and_Pensions "United States Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions") (HELP) held hearings on Kennedy's
