Kennedy disclosed to an HHS ethics official his arrangement with the law firm Wisner Baum, which specializes in pharmaceutical drug injury cases, under which Kennedy earns 10% of the fees awarded in contingency cases he refers to the firm. If confirmed as HHS director, Kennedy would retain the arrangement only in cases that do not directly affect the federal government.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:0-185)[[185]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-186) He listed his income from Wisner Baum for this arrangement as $856,559. Before assuming the position of director of HHS, he will receive from the law firm the complete and final payments for concluded cases against the US government.[[186]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-187)[*[needs update](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Manual_of_Style/Dates_and_numbers#Chronological_items "Wikipedia:Manual of Style/Dates and numbers")*] He added that will assign his son his interests in litigation against the maker of [Gardasil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gardasil "Gardasil"), a vaccine given to prevent [cervical cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervical_cancer "Cervical cancer") caused by [human papillomavirus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_papillomavirus "Human papillomavirus") (HPV).[[187]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-188)

On February 4, 2025, the Senate Committee on Finance voted 14–13 to forward Kennedy's nomination to a full Senate vote.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto11-189) The deciding vote was from [Bill Cassidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cassidy "Bill Cassidy"), who was originally hesitant, but said he had received "serious commitments" from the [Trump administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Second_presidency_of_Donald_Trump "Second presidency of Donald Trump") and "honest counsel" from Vice President [JD Vance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JD_Vance "JD Vance") in exchange for his support of Kennedy's nomination.[[188]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-auto11-189) According to the Senate HELP Committee site, Cassidy, a doctor who practiced for 30 years before becoming a politician, told the committee that he had had a patient with [acute hepatitis B](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acute_hepatitis_B "Acute hepatitis B") who needed a [liver transplant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver_transplant "Liver transplant") and had to be transported by [Medivac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_evacuation "Medical evacuation"). He called the transplant "an invasive, quarter-of-a-million-dollar surgery—in 2000—that, even if successful, would leave this young woman with a lifetime of $50,000 per year medical bills", adding, "As I saw her take off, I was so depressed. A $50 of vaccine could have prevented this all".[[189]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-190) Of the two committees that Kennedy spoke before, only the Senate Finance was to vote on his nomination.[[190]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-191)

On February 13, 2025, the Senate confirmed Kennedy as Secretary of Health and Human Services by a vote of 52 to 48, with former [Senate Republican Conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Senate_Republican_Conference "Senate Republican Conference") leader [Mitch McConnell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitch_McConnell "Mitch McConnell") the sole Republican to vote against him. A [polio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polio "Polio") survivor, McConnell was critical of efforts to revoke approval of the [polio vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polio_vaccine "Polio vaccine"). He said, "Anyone seeking the Senate's consent to serve in the incoming administration would do well to steer clear of even the appearance of association with such efforts." All Democrats also voted against Kennedy.[[191]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-192)

On March 16, 2026, Massachusetts District Court judge Brian Murphy ordered the reversal of all decisions made by the Advisory Committee for Immunization Practices by Kennedy-appointed panelists. Murphy found that the government had disregarded the [scientific method](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scientific_method "Scientific method") and "thereby undermined the integrity of its actions". His ruling was in response to a lawsuit brought by six medical organizations that contended Kennedy and his appointees had made "arbitrary and capricious" changes to the childhood vaccine schedule, bypassing the evidence-based practice that had underpinned it.[[192]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-193)

On August 19, 2026, U.S. District Judge [Christopher R. Cooper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_R._Cooper "Christopher R. Cooper") enjoined[[193]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-194) Kennedy from cutting HHS funding for evidence-based [teenage pregnancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage_pregnancy "Teenage pregnancy") prevention. The injunction was delivered partially because the decision to swap to programs based on [abstinence-only sex education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abstinence-only_sex_education "Abstinence-only sex education") and [teenage marriage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teenage_marriage "Teenage marriage") was justified with by [AI-generated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") research.[[194]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-195)[[195]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-196)

### Tenure

[https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/5/50/President_Trump_Participates_in_Swearing_in_Ceremony_for_the_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services_%282160p_60fps_VP9-128kbit_AAC%29.webm/President_Trump_Participates_in_Swearing_in_Ceremony_for_the_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services_%282160p_60fps_VP9-128kbit_AAC%29.webm.240p.vp9.webm](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/transcoded/5/50/President_Trump_Participates_in_Swearing_in_Ceremony_for_the_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services_%282160p_60fps_VP9-128kbit_AAC%29.webm/President_Trump_Participates_in_Swearing_in_Ceremony_for_the_Secretary_of_Health_and_Human_Services_%282160p_60fps_VP9-128kbit_AAC%29.webm.240p.vp9.webm)

Kennedy being sworn in as the [secretary of health and human services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_health_and_human_services "Secretary of health and human services") on February 13, 2025.

On February 13, 2025, Kennedy was sworn in as the 26th secretary of health and human services in the [Oval Office](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oval_Office "Oval Office") by Justice [Neil Gorsuch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Gorsuch "Neil Gorsuch").[[196]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-197) He is the first [independent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Independent_politician "Independent politician") or [third-party](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_party_(U.S._politics) "Third party (U.S. politics)") presidential candidate to become a [cabinet member](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States") after running for president.[[197]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-198)

#### "Make America Healthy Again" executive order

Minutes after Kennedy was sworn in, Trump signed Executive Order 14211, which ordered the creation of a "[Make America Healthy Again](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_America_Healthy_Again "Make America Healthy Again")" [(MAHA) Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MAHA_Commission "MAHA Commission") to be chaired by Kennedy.[[198]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-199)[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:9-200) Its objectives include investigating the incidence and causes of chronic childhood diseases and "assess[ing] the prevalence of and threat posed by the prescription of [selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Selective_serotonin_reuptake_inhibitor "Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor"), [antipsychotics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antipsychotic "Antipsychotic"), [mood stabilizers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mood_stabilizer "Mood stabilizer"), stimulants, and weight-loss drugs".[[199]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:9-200)

#### Firing staff

On February 14, 2025, agencies including the [Centers for Disease Control and Prevention](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Disease_Control_and_Prevention "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention") (CDC) and the [National Institutes of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institutes_of_Health "National Institutes of Health") (NIH) were informed that approximately 5,200 newly hired federal health workers were to be fired that day.[[200]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-201)

In April 2025, Kennedy fired most of the staff of the [National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_for_Occupational_Safety_and_Health "National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health"), shuttering nearly all its departments. Programs, including approvals of new workplace safety equipment and research into firefighter health, were abruptly canceled.[[201]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-202)

In June 2025, Kennedy announced that he was removing all 17 members of the [Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advisory_Committee_on_Immunization_Practices "Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices") (ACIP) and replacing them with new members.[[202]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-203) In May 2026, he fired two members of the [Preventive Services Task Force](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Preventive_Services_Task_Force "United States Preventive Services Task Force") panel.[[203]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-204)

#### Stopping ads for vaccine to reduce severity of seasonal flu

On February 20, 2025, during an unusually severe influenza season, HHS instructed the CDC to suspend its ad campaign promoting flu vaccination. The advertising, in part a response to declining flu vaccination rates, promoted the message that vaccination would result in much milder symptoms and lower chances of becoming severely ill for those with the flu.[[204]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-205)[[205]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-206)

#### 2025 Southwest United States measles outbreak

Main article: [2025 Southwest United States measles outbreak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Southwest_United_States_measles_outbreak "2025 Southwest United States measles outbreak")

Kennedy's tenure began during a measles outbreak in the southwestern US, including the first measles death in a decade. The [Texas Department of State Health Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Texas_Department_of_State_Health_Services "Texas Department of State Health Services") reported 146 cases, 20 hospitalizations, and one death in late February.[[206]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-207) In his first public comments, on February 26, Kennedy said there had been two deaths and that "there have been four measles outbreaks this year. In this country last year there were 16. So it's not unusual. We have measles outbreaks every year." Such outbreaks of the disease had been declared domestically eliminated until the [measles resurgence in the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measles_resurgence_in_the_United_States "Measles resurgence in the United States") that began in the 2010s.[[207]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-208) He also falsely claimed that the people hospitalized were done so "mainly for quarantine",[[208]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-209) a claim healthcare professionals refuted.[[209]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-210) US Senator [Ron Wyden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ron_Wyden "Ron Wyden") wrote: "Nothing about kids dying from measles is normal. Anti-vaxxers like RFK Jr. and the Republicans who enable them are responsible for every single one of these deaths."[[210]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-211)

Days later, Kennedy called the outbreak a "top priority" for the department.[[211]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-212) His messaging regarding the outbreak cited fringe theories blaming poor diet and health. He promoted [cod liver oil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cod_liver_oil "Cod liver oil"), steroid inhalation, an antibiotic, [vitamin A](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_A "Vitamin A"), and other questionable treatments that he called "almost miraculous". While recommending vaccination against measles, he also overstated the vaccine's potential harms and suggested that immunity from natural infection would be better. The CDC says that the MMR vaccine is "much safer than getting measles, mumps, or rubella". The antibiotic is not effective against a viral disease such as measles. Vitamin A is part of measles treatment, primarily in areas where children may be deficient in it.[[212]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-213)[[213]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-214)[[214]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-215)[[215]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-216)[[216]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-217)

On February 28, HHS's top spokesperson, Thomas Corry, abruptly resigned, two weeks after being sworn in as the assistant secretary of public affairs. He reportedly clashed with Kennedy over his management of the department during the measles outbreak.[[217]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-guard-3mar2025-218)[[218]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-pol-3mar2025-219)

On March 2, Kennedy was criticized for writing an op-ed for [Fox News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fox_News "Fox News") that called vaccines a "personal choice" and recommended vitamins and good nutrition to combat measles.[[219]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-guard-4mar2025-220) But he also wrote in the piece: "Vaccines not only protect individual children from measles, but also contribute to community immunity, protecting those who are unable to be vaccinated due to medical reasons."[[220]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-221)[[221]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-222)

After Kennedy took to the media to falsely claim that vitamin A is both a [prophylactic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prophylactic "Prophylactic") and treatment for measles, doctors in Texas began to see children infected with measles also having symptoms of [vitamin A toxicity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitamin_A_toxicity "Vitamin A toxicity").[[222]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-223)[[223]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-224)

On March 28, Kennedy told [Peter Marks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peter_Marks_(physician) "Peter Marks (physician)"), the head of the FDA's vaccine program, that he should resign or be fired. Marks wrote a resignation letter that lamented Kennedy's attempts to erode trust in vaccines: "It has become clear that truth and transparency are not desired by the secretary, but rather he wishes subservient confirmation of his misinformation and lies."[[224]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-marks-nytimes-225) Days earlier, the CDC head of communications said after his own resignation, "Kennedy and his team are working to bend science to fit their own narratives, rather than allowing facts to guide policy."[[225]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Griffis-226)

In April, Kennedy praised Texas doctor Ben Edwards as one of two "extraordinary healers" using unverified treatments for measles; the week before, Edwards was aware that he was infected with measles when he met children and parents at his clinic without wearing a mask.[[226]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-227)

After a second child died from measles in Texas in April, Kennedy said, "the most effective way to prevent the spread of measles is the MMR vaccine".[[227]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-228) Two days later, in an interview with CBS News, he said, "We encourage people to get the measles vaccine", adding that both his position and that of the federal government was that people should get the measles vaccine, although the government should not mandate it.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Kennedy_measles_vaccine-9)

#### MAHA report

Further information: [MAHA Commission](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MAHA_Commission "MAHA Commission") and [MAHA report](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/MAHA_report "MAHA report")

On May 22, 2025, the MAHA Commission released a report about childhood chronic disease.[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:12-229) It was described as "wide-ranging" and claimed that a range of factors, including diet, vaccinations, medical prescriptions, physical stress, food additives, and pesticides, are "potential drivers behind the rise in childhood chronic disease that present the clearest opportunities for progress".[[229]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-230)

On May 29, [NOTUS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NOTUS_(website) "NOTUS (website)") first reported that some of the studies the MAHA Commission's report cited did not exist; the authors of several other studies the report cited said their work was mischaracterized.[[230]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-231)[[231]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-232)[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:12-229) Medical researcher [Ivan Oransky](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ivan_Oransky "Ivan Oransky") said the errors were characteristic of [generative AI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Generative_AI "Generative AI") usage: "They come up with references that share a lot of words and authors and even journals, journal names, but they're not real."[[232]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-233) Some of the report's citation [URLs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/URLs "URLs") contained the string "oaicite", indicating a tool produced by [OpenAI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/OpenAI "OpenAI") was used.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:13-234)

[White House press secretary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_House_press_secretary "White House press secretary") [Karoline Leavitt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karoline_Leavitt "Karoline Leavitt") said these errors were "formatting issues that are being addressed and the report will be updated. But it does not negate the substance of the report, which, as you know, is one of the most transformative health reports that has ever been released by the federal government."[[234]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-235)[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:12-229) Asked whether the MAHA Commission's report used generative AI, Leavitt said, "I can't speak to that."[[228]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:12-229) The report was repeatedly updated that day.[[233]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:13-234) NOTUS released a follow-up addressing the updates and reported that while several errors from the original report had been edited or removed, new errors were found, including updated citations that misinterpret scientific studies.[[235]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-236)

#### CDC leadership departures

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/27/RFK_Jr._Takes_a_Chainsaw_to_the_CDC_to_Implement_His_MAHA_Agenda.jpg/250px-RFK_Jr._Takes_a_Chainsaw_to_the_CDC_to_Implement_His_MAHA_Agenda.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RFK_Jr._Takes_a_Chainsaw_to_the_CDC_to_Implement_His_MAHA_Agenda.jpg)A [political cartoon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Political_cartoon "Political cartoon") depicting Kennedy using a [chainsaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chainsaw "Chainsaw") labeled "[MAHA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Make_America_Healthy_Again "Make America Healthy Again")" to saw the sign of the [National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Center_for_Immunization_and_Respiratory_Diseases "National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases") (NCIRD) headquarters, in reference to the several oustings of NCIRD staff under his tenure

When CDC director [Susan Monarez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Susan_Monarez "Susan Monarez") was ousted in August 2025, several CDC leaders quit over Kennedy's anti-science policies. In a resignation note, [National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Center_for_Immunization_and_Respiratory_Diseases "National Center for Immunization and Respiratory Diseases") director [Demetre Daskalakis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Demetre_Daskalakis "Demetre Daskalakis") wrote that Kennedy and his appointees "threaten the lives of the youngest Americans and pregnant people". In a statement, lawyers for Monarez said that Kennedy had been "weaponizing public health for political gain" and "putting millions of American lives at risk". Houry's farewell announcement referenced vaccine misinformation, the 2025 [measles outbreak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#2025_Southwest_United_States_measles_outbreak), and the 2025 [shooting attack on the CDC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Disease_Control_and_Prevention#2025_headquarters_shooting "Centers for Disease Control and Prevention").[[236]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-237)[[237]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-238) Days after the departure, nine former CDC leaders from both Democratic and Republican administrations wrote in *The New York Times* that the shakeup at the agency was "unlike anything our country has ever experienced"[[238]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-239) and that Kennedy was "endangering every American's health."[[239]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-240)

#### Autism Data Science Initiative

On September 22, 2025, Kennedy approved a $50 million grant to the [National Institute of Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Health "National Institute of Health") (NIH) for 13 projects to "help transform autism research" through the proposed Autism Data Science Initiative.[[240]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-sept222025-241)[[241]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-242)

#### CDC revises stance on autism and vaccines

See also: [CDC § CDC revises stance on autism and vaccines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CDC#CDC_revises_stance_on_autism_and_vaccines "CDC")

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/df/P20250418MR-0680.jpg/250px-P20250418MR-0680.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:P20250418MR-0680.jpg)Kennedy swearing in [Mehmet Oz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mehmet_Oz "Mehmet Oz") as administrator of the [Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centers_for_Medicare_and_Medicaid_Services "Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services") on April 18, 2025

On November 19, 2025, the CDC website on "Autism and Vaccines" was radically changed from its September 2025 version.[[242]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-CDC_RFK_Autism_Vaccines_09/23/2025-243)[[243]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-CDC_RFK_Autism_Vaccines_11/19/2025-244) In an interview, Kennedy reportedly said that "he personally instructed the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to abandon its longstanding position that vaccines do not cause autism—a move that underscores his determination to challenge scientific consensus and bend the health department to his will."[[244]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Stolberg_11/21/2025-245)

[FactCheck.org](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FactCheck.org "FactCheck.org") wrote that the change was not evidence-based.[[245]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-McDonald_Yandell_11/20/2025-246) The revised site makes several false statements, contradicting longstanding scientific evidence that supports *the absence* of a causal link between childhood vaccines and autism.[[246]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-247) According to CDC staff, required scientific vetting for all public-facing agency webpages was entirely bypassed in this instance.[[247]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-248) The *Wall Street Journal* wrote, "no association has been proven between vaccines and autism".[[248]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-249) Numerous medical associations and professionals immediately issued statements protesting the changes, including experts from the [Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Center_for_Infectious_Disease_Research_and_Policy "Center for Infectious Disease Research and Policy") (CIDRAP); [Children's Hospital of Philadelphia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Children's_Hospital_of_Philadelphia "Children's Hospital of Philadelphia"); [Stanford University School of Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stanford_University_School_of_Medicine "Stanford University School of Medicine"); Texas Children's Hospital Center for Vaccine Development;[[249]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-250) the [American Academy of Pediatrics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_Academy_of_Pediatrics "American Academy of Pediatrics") (AAP); [Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvard_T.H._Chan_School_of_Public_Health "Harvard T.H. Chan School of Public Health"); and The Autism Science Foundation.[[250]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-251)[[251]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-252)

#### Hepatitis B vaccines

On December 5, 2025, Kennedy's [Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advisory_Committee_on_Immunization_Practices "Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices") (ACIP) vaccine panel voted to end the CDC's universal recommendation that newborn babies receive [Hepatitis B vaccine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepatitis_B_vaccine "Hepatitis B vaccine") doses and instead "recommend individual-based decision-making for parents deciding whether to give the hepatitis B vaccine, including the birth dose, to infants born to women who test negative for the virus. For those infants not receiving the birth dose, ACIP suggested in its recommendation that the initial dose be administered no earlier than two months of age".[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-hepbvaccine-253)[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-parentdecisionmaking-254)

The Kennedy-led ACIP also voted to "recommend that when evaluating the need for a subsequent hepatitis B vaccine dose in children, parents should consult with health care providers to decide whether to test antibody levels to hepatitis surface antigen to evaluate adequacy of protection through serology results."[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-hepbvaccine-253)[[253]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-parentdecisionmaking-254) This vote came "despite no evidence suggesting fewer doses than the standard series of three offer lifelong protection".[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-hepbvaccine-253)

Joseph Hibbeln, an ACIP member who voted against the change, said: "This has a great potential to cause harm, and I simply hope that the committee will accept its responsibility when this harm is caused."[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-hepbvaccine-253)

[Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate_Committee_on_Health,_Education,_Labor_and_Pensions "United States Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor and Pensions") chairman [Bill Cassidy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cassidy "Bill Cassidy") wrote: "Ending the recommendation for newborns makes it more likely the number of cases will begin to increase again. This makes America sicker."[[252]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-hepbvaccine-253)

Since 2005, Kennedy has promoted [vaccine misinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccine_misinformation "Vaccine misinformation")[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFKVaccineMisinformation-1) and public-health conspiracy theories,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFKConspiracySources-2) including the [chemtrail conspiracy theory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemtrail_conspiracy_theory "Chemtrail conspiracy theory"),[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-bbcChemtrails-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chemtrails-cnn-4) [HIV/AIDS denialism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HIV/AIDS_denialism "HIV/AIDS denialism"),[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFKAIDS-5) and the scientifically disproved claim of a causal link between [vaccines and autism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccines_and_autism "Vaccines and autism").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-FCRFKAutism-6) He has drawn criticism for fueling [vaccine hesitancy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaccine_hesitancy "Vaccine hesitancy") amid a social climate that gave rise to the deadly [measles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measles "Measles") outbreaks in [Samoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Samoa_measles_outbreak "2019 Samoa measles outbreak") and [Tonga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Tonga_measles_outbreak "2019 Tonga measles outbreak").[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-APMeaslesSamoa-7) In 2026, Kennedy drew criticism for [anti-Arab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-Arab_racism "Anti-Arab racism") remarks.[[254]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-255)[[255]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-256)

### Anti-vaccine advocacy and conspiracy theories on public health

Kennedy is a prominent voice in the anti-vaccine movement, spreading anti-vaccine [misinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Misinformation "Misinformation"), [disinformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disinformation "Disinformation"), and [propaganda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Propaganda "Propaganda").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-KW-40)[[256]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-mnookin-2017-257)[[257]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-NBC_2021-03-11-258)[[258]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Smith_12/15/2021-259)[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Time20230614-260) The infectious disease specialist [Michael Osterholm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Osterholm "Michael Osterholm") has said that Kennedy's "anti-vaccine disinformation" is effective "because it's portrayed to the public with graphs and figures and what appears to be scientific data. He has perfected the art of illusion of fact." Osterholm added:[[259]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Time20230614-260)
> This is about people's lives. And the consequences of promoting this kind of disinformation, as credible as it may seem, is simply dangerous.

Kennedy has said that he is not against vaccines but wants them to be more thoroughly tested and investigated.[[260]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-261)[[261]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-262) In *[Thimerosal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thiomersal "Thiomersal"): Let the Science Speak* (2015), he writes that he does not see himself as anti-vaccine: "People who advocate for safer vaccines should not be marginalized or denounced as anti-vaccine. I am pro-vaccine. I had all six of my children vaccinated. I believe that vaccines have saved the lives of hundreds of millions of humans over the past century and that broad vaccine coverage is critical to public health. But I want our vaccines to be as safe as possible."[[262]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-263) But in 2023, Kennedy said, "There's no vaccine that is safe and effective."[[263]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-264)[[264]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-265)

In January 2024, Kennedy published a podcast about [Lyme disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyme_disease "Lyme disease") in which he said it is "highly likely to have been a military weapon" developed at the [Plum Island Animal Disease Center](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plum_Island_Animal_Disease_Center "Plum Island Animal Disease Center"). Multiple experts and authoritative sources have debunked the charge and called it "absurd".[[265]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-266)

## Personal life

### General interests

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/RfkjrOCT2017.jpg/250px-RfkjrOCT2017.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:RfkjrOCT2017.jpg)Kennedy speaking at the Foro La Región in [Ourense, Spain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ourense,_Spain "Ourense, Spain") in 2017

Kennedy is a licensed master [falconer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Falconry "Falconry") and has trained hawks since he was 11. He breeds hawks and falcons and is also licensed as a raptor propagator and a wildlife rehabilitator.[[266]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-267) He holds permits for Federal [Game Keeper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Game_keeper "Game keeper"), [Bird Bander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_bander "Bird bander"), and Scientific Collector. He was president of the New York State Falconry Association from 1988 to 1991. In 1987, while on Governor [Mario Cuomo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mario_Cuomo "Mario Cuomo")'s New York State Falconry Advising Committee, Kennedy authored New York State's examination to qualify apprentice falconers. Later that year, he wrote the *New York State Apprentice Falconer's Manual*, which was published by the [New York State Department of Environmental Conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Department_of_Environmental_Conservation "New York State Department of Environmental Conservation") and remains in use.[[267]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-268)

Kennedy is also a [whitewater kayaker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitewater_kayaking "Whitewater kayaking"). His father introduced him and his siblings to whitewater kayaking during trips down the [Green](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Green_River_(Colorado_River) "Green River (Colorado River)") and [Yampa Rivers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yampa_River "Yampa River") in Utah and Colorado, the [Columbia River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_River "Columbia River"), the [Middle Fork Salmon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_Fork_Salmon_River "Middle Fork Salmon River") in Idaho, and the [Upper Hudson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Hudson "Upper Hudson") Gorge. Between 1976 and 1981, Kennedy was a partner and guide at a whitewater company, Utopian, based in [West Forks, Maine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/West_Forks,_Maine "West Forks, Maine"). He organized and led several "first-descent" whitewater expeditions to Latin America, including three hitherto unexplored rivers: the [Apurimac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apurímac_River "Apurímac River"), Peru, in 1975; the [Atrato](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrato "Atrato"), Colombia, in 1979; and the [Caroni](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroní_River "Caroní River"), Venezuela, in 1982.[[268]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-269) In 1993, he made an early descent of the [Great Whale River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Whale_River "Great Whale River") in northern Quebec, Canada.[[269]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-270)

In 2015, Kennedy took two of his sons to the [Yukon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yukon "Yukon") to visit [Mount Kennedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mount_Kennedy "Mount Kennedy") and run the [Alsek River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsek_River "Alsek River"), a whitewater river fed by the [Alsek Glacier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alsek_Glacier "Alsek Glacier"). Mount Kennedy was Canada's highest unclimbed peak when the Canadian government named it for John F. Kennedy in 1964.[[270]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-271) In 1965, Kennedy's father became the first person to climb Mount Kennedy.[[271]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-272)

### Marriages and children

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/8f/P20250213JB-0328_%28cropped%29.jpg/250px-P20250213JB-0328_%28cropped%29.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:P20250213JB-0328_(cropped).jpg)Kennedy with his third wife, [Cheryl Hines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Hines "Cheryl Hines"), in February 2025

On April 3, 1982, Kennedy married Emily Ruth Black, whom he met at the [University of Virginia School of Law](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Virginia_School_of_Law "University of Virginia School of Law").[[272]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-273) Kennedy and Black separated in 1992 and divorced in 1994.[[273]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-274)

On April 15, 1994, Kennedy married architect and designer [Mary Kathleen Richardson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Richardson_Kennedy "Mary Richardson Kennedy"), a close friend of his sister Kerry, aboard a research vessel on the [Hudson River](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hudson_River "Hudson River").[[274]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-275)[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-The_Guardian-17_May_2012-276) Kennedy has six children, two with Black and four with Richardson.[[276]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-277) His eldest child, [Robert F. Kennedy III](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_III "Robert F. Kennedy III"), is a director and screenwriter.[[277]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-278)[[278]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-279)[[279]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-280) Kennedy was given the nickname "Bobby" growing up.[[184]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:0-185)

During his marriage to Richardson, Kennedy was known among his friends for sending explicit nude photos of women that they presumed he had taken, according to *[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_Fair_(magazine) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")*.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hagan_20240702-32) He reportedly engaged in multiple affairs during the marriage.[[280]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-281)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hagan_20240702-32)[[281]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-282) His friends later called him a "lifelong philanderer".[[282]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-283)[[283]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-284) On May 12, 2010, Kennedy filed for divorce from Richardson. On May 16, 2012, Richardson was found dead in a building on the grounds of her home in [Bedford, New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bedford_(town),_New_York "Bedford (town), New York"). The Westchester County Medical Examiner ruled the death a [suicide due to asphyxiation from hanging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suicide_by_hanging "Suicide by hanging").[[284]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-285) The medical examiner's report noted her fingers were caught between the neck and the noose when she was found dead, indicating a struggle to free herself.[[285]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-286) Upon arriving at the scene, Richardson's sister told Kennedy, "you have killed my sister".[[286]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-287)

Before her death, Richardson had discovered Kennedy's personal journal from 2001, in which he recorded sexual encounters with 37 different women. According to Kennedy, Richardson passed the journal along "to her sisters with instructions that, if anything happened to her, [it should be] published in the press".[[287]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-288)[[288]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-289) During their divorce, Richardson began exhibiting signs of drug and alcohol abuse and psychiatric distress.[[275]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-The_Guardian-17_May_2012-276)[[289]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-290)[[290]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-291)

After her death, Kennedy won a court case against Richardson's siblings to have her buried alongside fellow Kennedy family members in St. Francis Xavier Cemetery in [Centerville, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centerville,_Massachusetts "Centerville, Massachusetts"), instead of closer to her siblings in New York. Shortly after her burial, Kennedy had her body disinterred and moved to an unmarked grave in an empty area of the cemetery. At the time, the Kennedy family was planning to purchase 50 plots in the same area due to overcrowding.[[291]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-292) Kennedy's niece Saoirse Kennedy Hill was buried next to Richardson after her death from a drug overdose at age 22.[[292]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-293)

In 2011, Kennedy began dating the actress [Cheryl Hines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cheryl_Hines "Cheryl Hines"). They married on August 2, 2014, at the [Kennedy Compound](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_Compound "Kennedy Compound"). The couple were introduced by [Larry David](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larry_David "Larry David"), Hines's co-star on [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO")'s *[Curb Your Enthusiasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Curb_Your_Enthusiasm "Curb Your Enthusiasm")*.[[293]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-294)[[294]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-295)[[295]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-296) Kennedy and Hines reside in [Los Angeles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles")[[296]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-297) and [Cape Cod, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cape_Cod,_Massachusetts "Cape Cod, Massachusetts").[[297]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-298)

In September 2024, [Olivia Nuzzi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olivia_Nuzzi "Olivia Nuzzi"), a reporter for *[New York](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_(magazine) "New York (magazine)")* magazine who had been covering his presidential campaign, told her editors that she had been in a relationship with Kennedy, which she described as personal but not physical.[[298]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-299)[[299]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-300)[[300]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-301)[[301]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-302)

### Health

During Kennedy's college years, he began having heart problems, which he has said were caused by [caffeine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caffeine "Caffeine"), [stress](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psychological_stress "Psychological stress"), and [sleep deprivation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sleep_deprivation "Sleep deprivation").[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:6-303)

In his 40s, Kennedy developed adductor [spasmodic dysphonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spasmodic_dysphonia "Spasmodic dysphonia"), an organic voice disorder that causes his voice to quaver and makes speech difficult. It is a form of involuntary movement affecting the [larynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larynx "Larynx"), related to [dystonia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dystonia "Dystonia").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-KW-40)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-living-dangerously-43)[[303]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-voice-disorder-304) Kennedy said he traveled to [Kyoto](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kyoto "Kyoto"), Japan, for a procedure where a titanium bridge was inserted between his vocal cords to try to relieve the disorder.[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:6-303)

Kennedy began experiencing severe short- and long-term memory loss and [mental fog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mental_fog "Mental fog") in 2010. In a 2012 divorce court deposition, he attributed neurological issues to "a worm that got into my brain and ate a portion of it and then died", in addition to [mercury poisoning](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mercury_poisoning "Mercury poisoning") from eating large quantities of tuna.[[302]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-:6-303)[[304]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-305) *The Washington Post* reported that Kennedy's campaign "has not released his medical records that could verify his account, and Kennedy has previously spread health misinformation, including about mercury in vaccines".[[305]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Nirappil-306)

### Religion

Kennedy is a [Roman Catholic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catholic_Church "Catholic Church").[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-globe1-307) In 2005, journalist [Michael Paulson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Paulson "Michael Paulson") called him "a deeply devout Catholic who attends daily Mass".[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chron1-308) Kennedy considers [Francis of Assisi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_of_Assisi "Francis of Assisi") his patron saint and a role model.[[306]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-globe1-307) In a 2005 interview with *[The Boston Globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Boston_Globe "The Boston Globe")*, he said he was deeply inspired by Francis's devotion to [social justice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Social_justice "Social justice"), [helping the poor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poverty_relief "Poverty relief"), [animal welfare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_welfare "Animal welfare"), and [environmentalism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Environmentalism "Environmentalism"); Francis is a [patron saint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patron_saint "Patron saint") of [ecology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecology "Ecology").[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chron1-308)

In 2004, Kennedy published a biography, *Saint Francis of Assisi: A Life of Joy*.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chron1-308) He said Catholicism was a vehicle of his environmentalism, adding, "environmental work is spiritual work".[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chron1-308) Despite identifying as [pro-life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pro-life "Pro-life"),[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chron1-308) Kennedy also identifies with [liberal Catholicism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progressive_Christianity "Progressive Christianity").[[308]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-unherd1-309) He criticized the church's argument that [John Kerry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Kerry "John Kerry") should have been denied communion because of his support for abortion rights.[[307]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-chron1-308)

In a 2018 interview with *[Vatican News](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vatican_News "Vatican News")*, Kennedy expressed his admiration for [Pope John XXIII](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pope_John_XXIII "Pope John XXIII"), who is best known for his modernization of the church in the 1960s. Kennedy said, "the Church should be an instrument of justice and kindness around the world."[[309]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-vat1-310)

### Sexual assault allegations

In July 2024, *[Vanity Fair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vanity_Fair_(magazine) "Vanity Fair (magazine)")* reported that in the late 1990s, when he was in his 40s, Kennedy engaged in [sexual misconduct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_misconduct "Sexual misconduct") with Eliza Cooney, a 23-year-old part-time babysitter for his children.[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-BBConVF-311) Cooney alleges that Kennedy groped her and touched her inappropriately on multiple occasions and asked her to rub lotion on his back when the two were alone in a bedroom.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hagan_20240702-32)

Kennedy called this *Vanity Fair* piece a "lot of garbage". When asked specifically about Cooney's allegation, he responded, "I am not a church boy. I had a very, very rambunctious youth. I said in my announcement speech that I have so many skeletons in my closet that if they could all vote, I could run for king of the world." When pressed further, he said he had no comment.[[310]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-BBConVF-311)

After the *Vanity Fair* piece was published, Cooney said that Kennedy texted her: "I have no memory of this incident, but I apologize sincerely for anything I ever did that made you feel uncomfortable or anything I did or said that offended you or hurt your feelings. I never intended you any harm. If I hurt you, it was inadvertent. I feel badly for doing so."[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Mansfield-312) Cooney said, "I don't know if it's an apology if you say 'I don't remember' ... In the context of all his public appearances, it seemed a little bit—it didn't match. It was like a throwaway."[[311]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Mansfield-312)

### Relationship with Jeffrey Epstein

See also: [List of people named in the Epstein files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_people_named_in_the_Epstein_files "List of people named in the Epstein files")

In August 2025, [Ghislaine Maxwell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ghislaine_Maxwell "Ghislaine Maxwell") said Kennedy was among those who traveled with [Jeffrey Epstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeffrey_Epstein "Jeffrey Epstein"), a claim backed by travel logs released during Maxwell's 2021 trial, though she said she "never saw anything inappropriate" from him during that time.[[312]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-313) In response, Kennedy initially claimed that he had flown only once on [Epstein's plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lolita_Express "Lolita Express") for a family Easter trip, only to later confirm a second instance in which he joined Epstein for a fossil hunting trip to [South Dakota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_Dakota "South Dakota").[[313]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-314)[[314]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-315)[[315]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-316)

In November 2025, Kennedy was confirmed to be among those listed in Epstein's personal contact book.[[316]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-317) The release of the [Epstein Files](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_Files "Epstein Files") under the [Epstein Files Transparency Act](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epstein_Files_Transparency_Act "Epstein Files Transparency Act") included an email from Epstein replying "whoops" to an email from an associate informing him of Richardson Kennedy's death.[[317]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-318) Kennedy has dismissed his ties to Epstein as merely social, pointing to his similarly knowing sexual predators [Harvey Weinstein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harvey_Weinstein "Harvey Weinstein") and [Bill Cosby](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Cosby "Bill Cosby"), among others.[[318]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-319)

### Treatment of dead animals

In July 2024, an image of Kennedy holding a charred animal carcass captured in 2010 surfaced in a *Vanity Fair* story, which alleged that the carcass belonged to a dog and that Kennedy ate it.[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hagan_20240702-32) Kennedy denied that he ate [dog meat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog_meat "Dog meat"), and said the animal carcass in the picture was a goat.[[319]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-320) According to *[Snopes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snopes "Snopes")*, the carcass in the photo is lamb.[[320]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-321) Kennedy had eaten dog, [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_meat "Horse meat"), and [guinea pig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Guinea_pig "Guinea pig") meat before 2001.[[321]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-322)

In August 2024, Kennedy released a video on [X (formerly Twitter)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/X_(social_network) "X (social network)"), acknowledging that in October 2014 he placed a dead six-month-old bear in [Central Park](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Park "Central Park") after initially planning to skin it for [meat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear_hunting#Meat "Bear hunting").[[322]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-323) Kennedy said that the bear had been [hit by a car](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Roadkill "Roadkill") in front of him and that he ultimately abandoned the carcass for fear that it would decay before he could preserve it, deliberately positioning the body to give the impression that it had been struck by a cyclist in Central Park.[[323]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-RFKJ_Bear_Treisman_2024-324) He released the video in advance of a story in *[The New Yorker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_Yorker "The New Yorker")* that detailed the incident.[[324]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-325) At the time of the incident, the spectacle of a dead bear in a New York City park made the local news. A resulting [necropsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necropsy "Necropsy") by the [New York State Department of Environmental Conservation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_York_State_Department_of_Environmental_Conservation "New York State Department of Environmental Conservation") found that the death was caused by "[blunt force injuries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blunt_force_injuries "Blunt force injuries") consistent with a motor vehicle collision".[[325]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-326)

In a 2012 *Town & Country* magazine profile of Kennedy's daughter Kathleen ("Kick"), she recounted a story about how her father—who, she said, liked to study animal skulls and skeletons—used a chainsaw to sever the head of a dead [beached whale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetacean_stranding "Cetacean stranding") in [Hyannis Port, Massachusetts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyannis_Port,_Massachusetts "Hyannis Port, Massachusetts"), then strapped the whale's head to the top of their minivan with bungee cords for the five-hour drive home, saying, "every time we accelerated on the highway, whale juice would pour into the windows of the car" and they "had plastic bags over our heads with mouth holes cut out, and people on the highway were giving us the finger, but that was just normal day-to-day stuff for us".[[326]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-Hudson-25_Dec_2012-327) In 2024, an environmental advocacy group asked the [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Fisheries Office of Law Enforcement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration_Fisheries_Office_of_Law_Enforcement "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Fisheries Office of Law Enforcement") to investigate possible violations of the [Marine Mammal Protection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_Mammal_Protection_Act "Marine Mammal Protection Act") and [Endangered Species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endangered_Species_Act "Endangered Species Act") laws. The agency determined the allegation was unfounded.[[327]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-328)[[328]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-329)[[329]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-330)

According to [Isabel Vincent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Isabel_Vincent "Isabel Vincent")'s 2026 book *RFK Jr: The Fall and Rise*, Kennedy wrote in his November 11, 2001, diary entry that he had cut the penis off a road-killed raccoon.[[330]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-331) Vincent writes that Kennedy took the raccoon's genitals so he could "study them later".[[331]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_F._Kennedy_Jr.#cite_note-332)
